item.title: 🔴 Rapid7 Analysis: Unauthenticated File Upload to RCE in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764)
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.

Overview

An origin-validation flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support lets an unauthenticated attacker write files on the appliance and execute code as the site's operating-system user. The entry point is the public customer connection used to start a support session. No account credentials or user interaction are required.

The flaw sits between the internal message router, brain, and an appliance-side customer worker, thin-scc. An attacker can put a reserved local router ID into a message's source address. The router forwards the message, and the worker accepts that address as proof that the request came from a local component. This gives the attacker access to an internal file-transfer service, including its native filesystem provider.

item.title: 🔴 php2shell one week later: Why one exploit doesn’t work everywhere
item.description:
Why this matters: Remote-code-execution risk — assess exposure and patch or mitigate quickly.

php2shell raised fears of mass exploitation. A week of testing by our research team found that working exploits had to be fitted to each target’s exact PHP setup. Systems that share one build, such as network appliances, are the exception: one tuned exploit can reach every device that runs it.

Key takeaways

  1. The five vulnerable PHP sites we exposed to the internet were not compromised, and public proofs-of-concept (PoCs) that go beyond version checks do not reliably confirm whether a host is vulnerable. Exploitation has been confirmed elsewhere, on researcher honeypots and on some network appliances.
  2. In realistic environments, turning php2shell into remote code execution usually takes an exploit built for the specific target. That is hard, not impossible, and it puts php2shell in a different category from Log4Shell, even though both received near-maximum severity ratings. Where many systems share one build, such as network appliances, a single calibrated exploit can work against all of them.
  3. Patch now, starting with internet-facing management interfaces, network appliances, and end-of-life PHP branches. Tenable Nessus and Tenable One Web App Scanning have had version-based detection since October 21.

item.title: 🔴 Whole-of-state defense: How SLED agencies can secure critical infrastructure in the AI era
item.description:
Why this matters: Elevated ransomware risk — validate backups, endpoint protection, and recovery readiness.

AI is widening the attack surface of the critical infrastructure facilities and services that state, local, and education (SLED) organizations run. In the final post of our Cybersecurity Awareness Month series, we explain how a whole-of-state security approach can help SLED agencies protect their critical infrastructure.

Key takeaways

  1. Because cyber attackers prey on under-resourced targets, they often go after SLED organizations, especially those that operate critical infrastructure, including water systems, hospitals, mass transit, emergency services, and schools. 
  2. In the latest research from the National Association of State Chief Information Officers (NASCIO), nearly 90% of state CIOs rated cyberattacks on critical systems as a high concern.
  3. AI expands the attack surface in two fundamental ways: SLED agencies and employees adopt AI tools and AI-built apps faster than security teams can authorize and inventory them, while attackers use AI automation to find weak points faster.
  4. A whole-of-state cybersecurity approach treats state agencies, counties, cities, school districts, and utilities as one defensive perimeter, with shared visibility, shared services, and clear governance.

Cyber attackers often look for the weakest link that can offer them an entry point into larger targets. If they can’t crack a state agency’s hardened systems, they’ll try to breach it in a roundabout way by first breaking into a small town…

Source: Tenable Blog  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 3d
